text.en: The Pallavas combined a centralised monarchy with decentralised local governance.
A king who made a tax-free land grant stopped being the supreme head of the state.
Villages that received tax-free land grants from the Pallavas were known as Brahmadeya villages.
Some Chālukya agrahārams, such as those at Aihole and Badami, became prominent centres of learning.

explanation.en: The Pallava king stayed the supreme head of state while the kingdom was divided into provinces, districts, taluks and villages. His tax-free grants made Brahmadeya villages. The Chālukyas of Badami gave land to Brahmin settlements called agrahārams, and those at Aihole and Badami became prominent centres of learning.

hints.en: A grant gave up the tax from one place. Ask whether that ended the king's position.
Brahmadeya is the Pallava word, and agrahāram is the Chālukya word.
